en.title: k in key (/k/)
en.summary: This item illustrates the letter k representing the sound /k/ as in the word key.

sections.title: Sounds of Che and Chi
paragraphs: The letter group is called /ke/, /ki/. Its main sound is heard in (chelner) /kʲe̯e/, which means key. This spelling represents two sound variants in Romanian.

sections.title: How to Say It
paragraphs: For the first sound, press the middle of your tongue against the hard roof of your mouth. Release the air suddenly without any voice. For the second variant, make the same crisp stop at the end of a word, but add a soft breath. Hold your palm near your lips to feel that tiny puff of air.

sections.title: Spelling Rules
paragraphs: Before e or i, the letters make the sound /kʲ/, that is a soft k before a vowel. You hear this in (cheie) /ˈkʲe.je/. At the very end of a word, the group makes the sound /kʲ/, that is a soft k whisper. You can hear it in (vechi) /vekʲ/.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
paragraphs: Do not pronounce this group like the ch in cheese. It is always a hard, soft k sound, like the k in kitchen. Keep your tongue high against the roof of your mouth. Do not add an English w sound after it.
